name: Heart-healthy Asian
summary: A week of bright, fragrant Asian home cooking built to stay low in sodium and saturated fat: brown rice, tofu and edamame, fish three times, and ginger, garlic, scallion, lime and chili doing the seasoning. Soy sauce, miso and fish sauce are kept to teaspoons, so it still tastes full.
howItWorks:
**Flavour without the salt.** Ginger, garlic, scallion, lemongrass, lime, rice vinegar, chili, sesame, star anise and cilantro do most of the seasoning. Soy sauce, miso and fish sauce stay in the dishes, but as teaspoons, and always paired with acid or heat.

**Fish, soy and whole grains.** Salmon on Tuesday, mackerel on Thursday and trout on Sunday bring omega-3, and they're always cooked fresh. Tofu, edamame and soy milk carry plant protein, while brown rice, barley, oats and buckwheat soba keep the starch mostly whole-grain. Cook a double pot of rice and barley on Sunday and keep it 4 days; freeze the rest.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's shrimp and tofu, Wednesday's tofu stir-fry, Friday's tofu stew and Saturday's pho each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is done. At Light the second snack drops and there's a little less oil and noodles, while the fish and tofu stay the same; at Big a snack is added each day.

**Shop for low sodium.** Choose reduced-sodium soy sauce, low-sodium broth, calcium-set firm tofu, plain peeled shrimp and unsalted peanuts, and cook noodles in unsalted water. Fish sauce and miso are a splash, not a pour.

**A note on your care team.** If you take blood-pressure or heart medication, follow your care team's advice. This plan is just built to be low in sodium and saturated fat.

recipes.name: Toasted sesame oats with soy milk and tangerine
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese sesame sweets and porridges
recipes.about: Creamy oats cooked in soy milk with a pinch of cinnamon and fresh ginger, topped with toasted sesame, juicy tangerine segments and a drizzle of honey. It tastes nutty and warming, a bit like a Japanese sesame sweet. The **oats and soy milk give slow, steady energy** and a good dose of plant protein.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until they smell nutty and start to pop. Crush about half of them with the back of a spoon.
Put the oats, soy milk, cinnamon and ginger in a small pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the tangerine segments, the whole sesame and a drizzle of honey. Stir the crushed sesame through the top.
recipes.tip: Cook a double batch and reheat a portion the next day with a splash of soy milk.

recipes.name: Egg scramble with shiitake and spinach on toast
recipes.inspiredBy: Hong Kong-style scrambled eggs on toast, with mushrooms and spinach
recipes.about: Fluffy eggs folded with browned shiitake, wilted spinach and scallion, served on toast with a tangerine. A few drops of soy sauce and sesame oil make it taste rich and savoury with very little salt. **Eggs and mushrooms bring protein and choline** to the start of your day.

ingredients.note: sliced, whites and greens kept apart

steps: Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the shiitake and cook, stirring only now and then, until browned and shrunk, about 4 minutes.
Add the scallion whites and spinach and stir until the spinach just wilts, about 1 minute.
Pour in the beaten eggs and push them gently around the pan until no runny egg is left and they are firm all through, about 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and finish with the soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper and scallion greens. Serve on the toast with the tangerine on the side.
recipes.tip: Segment the tangerine the night before to keep the morning quick.

recipes.name: Ginger shiitake brown rice congee with tofu and peanuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese jook and Cantonese congee
recipes.about: A slow-simmered, silky brown rice porridge with ginger and shiitake, with cubes of tofu stirred in at the end and finished with scallion, toasted sesame oil and crunchy peanuts. It's the weekend breakfast that makes the house smell wonderful. The **whole-grain rice and tofu are filling**, and the ginger and white pepper add warmth instead of salt.

ingredients.note: sliced into coins and fine matchsticks

steps: Rinse the rice. Put it in a pot with the broth, the ginger coins, the shiitake and enough water to bring the total liquid, broth included, to about 12 times the weight of the rice. Bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, partly cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the rice has burst and the congee is thick and creamy. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Fish out the ginger coins, then stir in the tofu and let it warm through for 2 minutes.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the ginger matchsticks, scallion, peanuts, sesame oil, white pepper and the soy sauce.
recipes.tip: Make a double pot and reheat with a splash of water. It keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Cold soba with edamame and sesame-ginger dressing
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese zaru soba and cold sesame noodles
recipes.about: Chewy buckwheat noodles tossed with plenty of edamame and crisp cucumber in a tangy rice vinegar, ginger and toasted sesame dressing. It's cool, crunchy and quick, and a teaspoon of soy sauce carries the flavour. **Edamame brings protein and folate**, so it eats like a full lunch.

ingredients.note: fresh, from the refrigerated case; dried works, but check the label for salt

steps: Boil the edamame in plenty of unsalted water for 3 minutes, then add the soba for the last 2 to 3 minutes, or as the packet says. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool, then drain well.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, canola oil, sesame oil, ginger, lime juice and chili flakes in a large bowl.
Add the noodles, edamame, cucumber and most of the scallion. Toss gently.
Pile into a bowl and top with the sesame seeds and the rest of the scallion.
recipes.tip: Make the dressing the night before. The noodles are best tossed just before you eat.

recipes.name: Ginger-garlic tofu with broccoli, shiitake and carrot
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese home-style stir-fried tofu with vegetables
recipes.about: Golden pan-seared tofu tossed in a light ginger, garlic and rice vinegar glaze with broccoli, shiitake and carrot, served over chewy brown rice and barley. A little reduced-sodium soy sauce does the seasoning, and **garlic, ginger and chili do the rest**. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, check the label; pressed dry and cut into cubes

steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes, and let them rest off the heat for 10 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, broth and chili flakes in a small bowl.
Heat half the canola oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning now and then, until golden on most sides, about 8 minutes. Lift it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli, carrot and shiitake. Stir-fry for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and scallion and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 3 to 4 minutes into a light glaze. Return the tofu and toss to coat, then finish with the sesame oil and serve over the rice and barley.
Pack the second portion, with its share of the grains, for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: Rice and barley freeze flat in bags and reheat in 2 minutes.

recipes.name: Ginger-scallion salmon with bok choy and brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Cantonese ginger-scallion sauce, made with far less salt
recipes.about: Roasted salmon under a bright pile of fresh ginger and scallion, finished with a hot sizzle of oil and a splash of rice vinegar and soy. Silky bok choy and a chewy brown rice and barley mix soak up the juices. **Salmon is rich in omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the whole plate is built on fresh aromatics instead of salt.

ingredients.note: skin on or off, as you like

steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Put the salmon on a lined tray, pat it dry and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until it just flakes.
Meanwhile, steam the bok choy over simmering water for 3 to 4 minutes, until the stems are tender but still bright green. Lay it on a platter.

Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chili flakes. Put the ginger, scallion and garlic in a small heatproof bowl. Heat the canola oil until shimmering and pour it over the aromatics: it will sizzle. Stir in the sesame oil.
Lay the salmon on the bok choy, spoon the sizzled aromatics over it and drizzle with the soy mixture. Serve with the rice and barley.
recipes.tip: Rice and barley freeze flat in bags and reheat in 2 minutes.

recipes.name: Vietnamese chicken, cabbage and cilantro salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Vietnamese goi ga, chicken and cabbage salad
recipes.about: Poached chicken, shredded cabbage, carrot and rice vermicelli tossed in a lime, garlic and chili dressing, with cilantro and crushed peanuts on top. It's cool, crunchy and tangy-sweet, with a little fish sauce for depth. The **chicken is lean and high in protein**, and the cilantro and cabbage bring vitamins C and K.
steps: Put the chicken in a small pot with enough cold water to cover. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for about 15 minutes, until cooked through. Lift it out and shred it with two forks.
Meanwhile, soak or boil the vermicelli in unsalted water until tender, about 4 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic and chili flakes until smooth.
Toss the chicken, noodles, cabbage, carrot and cucumber with the dressing. Fold in the cilantro, then top with the peanuts.
recipes.tip: Poach two breasts at once. The shredded chicken keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Lemongrass-chili shrimp and tofu with broccoli and brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Vietnamese tom xao sa ot, lemongrass-chili shrimp
recipes.about: Plump shrimp and golden tofu stir-fried with lemongrass, garlic and chili, tossed with broccoli and carrot and finished with lime and a little fish sauce. It's fragrant, sharp and fresh, and the brown rice and barley soak up the pan juices. **Shrimp is lean and rich in selenium**, and plain peeled shrimp keeps the sodium in check.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, pressed dry and cut into cubes

steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, honey and chili flakes in a small bowl.

Heat half the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu until golden, about 6 minutes. Lift it onto a plate. Turn the heat to high, sear the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes a side, until just pink, and add them to the plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the broccoli and carrot. Stir-fry for 4 minutes, adding a splash of water if the pan dries, then add the lemongrass and garlic for the last minute.
Return the tofu and shrimp, pour in the sauce and toss for 30 seconds. Serve over the rice and barley, topped with cilantro and peanuts.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch and reheat it gently, or eat it at room temperature.
recipes.tip: Skip the chili flakes for a milder dish, and add extra lime at the end.

recipes.name: Miso-ginger mackerel with sesame spinach and brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese saba misoyaki (miso-glazed mackerel) and spinach goma-ae
recipes.about: Mackerel brushed with a thin miso, honey and ginger glaze, broiled until the edges caramelize, with sesame spinach and a squeeze of lime. A small spoon of miso gives deep savoury flavour, and rice vinegar brightens it. **Mackerel is among the richest sources of omega-3** and also brings vitamin D.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes.
Whisk the miso, honey, half the ginger and half the rice vinegar into a loose paste.

Heat the broiler to high. Lay the mackerel skin side up on a lined tray and broil about 10 cm from the heat for 4 minutes. Flip it, brush the paste thinly over the flesh and broil 3 minutes more, until the glaze browns in spots and the fish flakes.

Meanwhile, blanch the spinach in boiling water for 40 seconds, then cool it under cold water, squeeze out the water and cut it into short lengths. Toss with the sesame oil, soy sauce, the rest of the rice vinegar and ginger, and half the sesame seeds.
Serve the mackerel on the rice and barley with the spinach alongside. Squeeze the lime over the fish and finish with the scallion and the rest of the sesame.
recipes.tip: Atlantic mackerel is easier to find and works just as well. Salmon or trout fillets also take the glaze.

recipes.name: Lemongrass chicken noodle bowl with cilantro and lime
recipes.inspiredBy: Vietnamese bun thit nuong, with a lighter dressing
recipes.about: Thinly sliced chicken breast seared with lemongrass and garlic, piled over rice vermicelli with cucumber, cabbage and carrot, lots of cilantro and crushed peanuts, with a bright lime and chili dressing. It's fresh, crunchy and bright. **Chicken breast is lean and high in protein**, and the cilantro and cabbage add vitamin K.
steps: Toss the chicken with the lemongrass, half the garlic, the canola oil, half of the fish sauce and half of the honey from the dressing, and let it sit while you prepare everything else.
Soak or boil the vermicelli in unsalted water until tender, about 4 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the lime juice with the rest of the fish sauce, honey and garlic and the chili flakes to make the dressing.

Sear the chicken in a hot non-stick pan for 4 to 5 minutes, until browned and cooked through, with no pink inside and a thermometer reading 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.
Layer the noodles, cucumber, cabbage and carrot in a bowl. Top with the chicken, cilantro and peanuts and pour the dressing over.
recipes.tip: Slice the chicken the night before so it is already marinating when you get home.

recipes.name: Korean-style tofu, mushroom and egg stew
recipes.inspiredBy: Korean sundubu-jjigae, with firm tofu and less salt
recipes.about: A bubbling red stew of tender tofu, shiitake and bok choy with a firm-set egg in a garlicky chili broth, with a small bowl of brown rice and barley. A little gochujang and gochugaru give it that deep Korean heat, and a splash of toasted sesame oil finishes it. The **tofu and egg carry the protein**, and the shiitake add umami.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, broken into large pieces by hand
sliced, whites and greens kept apart

steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Warm the canola oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the white parts of the scallion, the garlic and the gochugaru and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Stir in the gochujang and fish sauce, then pour in the broth, add the shiitake and bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and the bok choy. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, then season with the soy sauce.

Crack tonight's share of the eggs into the stew, cover and cook for about 4 minutes, until the whites and the yolks are both firm, about 4 minutes. Keep tomorrow's share in the shell and crack it in when you reheat. Finish with the sesame oil and the scallion greens and serve with the rice and barley.
Pack the second portion, with its grains, for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: Add a handful of spinach or napa cabbage at the end for extra greens.

recipes.name: Chicken pho with charred ginger, star anise and cilantro
recipes.inspiredBy: Vietnamese pho ga, with a lighter broth
recipes.about: A fragrant, clear broth built on charred onion and ginger, star anise, cinnamon and coriander seed, with tender chicken, rice noodles, shiitake, bok choy and a handful of cilantro and lime at the table. It's a weekend project that makes two bowls, and tomorrow's lunch tastes even deeper. Because the **spices and charred aromatics make the broth**, it needs only a little fish sauce.
steps: Char the onion halves and the ginger directly on a gas flame, under the broiler or in a dry cast-iron pan for about 10 minutes, turning, until blackened in spots. Peel off the worst of the black skin.

Toast the star anise and coriander seed in a dry pot for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the cinnamon, the charred onion and ginger, the shiitake, the broth and enough water to make about 450 ml of broth for each bowl. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently, partly covered, for 30 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until just cooked through. Lift it out, rest it for 5 minutes and slice it thinly.

Line a fine sieve with a damp paper towel and strain the broth through it back into the pot; the towel catches the ground cinnamon and keeps the broth clear. Stir in the fish sauce. Pick the shiitake out of the sieve and return it to the pot. Keep it at a gentle simmer and blanch the bok choy for 1 minute.
Cook the noodles in unsalted water until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Fill one bowl with noodles, chicken, shiitake and bok choy and ladle the hot broth over. Serve with the cabbage, cilantro, scallion, chili flakes and lime at the table.
Keep the second portion's broth separate from its cold noodles and toppings in the fridge. Reheat the broth until steaming and pour it over them tomorrow.
recipes.tip: Flat rice noodles (banh pho) are traditional if your store has them. A few torn mint or Thai basil leaves and an extra squeeze of lime at the table are lovely, and add no salt.

recipes.name: Thai-style steamed trout with lime, garlic and chili
recipes.inspiredBy: Thai steamed fish with lime (pla neung manao)
recipes.about: Tender steamed trout spooned with a sharp, hot lime, garlic and chili sauce and a handful of cilantro, with carrot, broccoli and brown rice and barley. It's a fresh, punchy take on Thai pla neung manao that needs only a little fish sauce. **Trout gives you omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the lime sauce does the work salt usually does.
steps: Start the grains: rinse the rice and barley together, then simmer them covered in about two and a half times their volume of water for about 40 minutes and rest them off the heat for 10 minutes.
Mix the lime juice, garlic, chili flakes, fish sauce and honey, stirring until the honey dissolves. Taste: it should be sharp, a little sweet and hot.

Put the lemongrass and ginger in a steamer set over simmering water. Lay the trout on top with the carrot alongside, cover and steam for 7 to 9 minutes, until the fish just flakes. Add the broccoli for the last 5 minutes.
Lift the trout, broccoli and carrot onto a plate and spoon the lime sauce over them. Scatter with the cilantro, scallion and peanuts and serve with the rice and barley.
recipes.tip: Use a bamboo steamer, or a heatproof plate set on a rack inside a lidded pot.

recipes.name: Chili-lime edamame
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese edamame, with lime and chili in place of salt
recipes.about: Warm edamame tossed with lime juice, chili flakes and toasted sesame. It's quick, salt-free and a great little hit of protein. **Edamame is a complete plant protein** with plenty of folate and fibre.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 to 4 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lime juice, chili flakes and sesame seeds while still warm.

recipes.name: Pineapple with toasted walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: the fruit plate after a Chinese family dinner, with toasted walnuts
recipes.about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a small handful of walnuts toasted until fragrant. It's sweet, juicy and crunchy, and it's ready in five minutes. The **walnuts add plant omega-3** and the pineapple adds vitamin C.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Serve with the pineapple.

recipes.name: Chilled tofu with ginger and scallion
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese hiyayakko
recipes.about: A cool slab of tofu topped with grated ginger, scallion, toasted sesame and a few drops of soy sauce. It's clean-tasting and savoury, and it takes two minutes. The **tofu gives protein and calcium**.
steps: Slide the tofu onto a small plate and pat the top dry.
Top with the ginger, scallion and sesame seeds, then drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil.
recipes.tip: Silken tofu is the classic and softer choice; firm, calcium-set tofu holds its shape and carries more calcium.

recipes.name: Pineapple with lime, chili and peanuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Southeast Asian fruit with chili and lime
recipes.about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a squeeze of lime, a pinch of chili and a small handful of unsalted peanuts. It's sweet, sour, hot and crunchy at once. The **pineapple brings vitamin C** and the peanuts bring protein and vitamin E.
steps: Toss the pineapple with the lime juice and chili flakes.
Sprinkle with the peanuts.

recipes.name: Carrot sticks with peanut-lime dip
recipes.inspiredBy: Vietnamese peanut dipping sauce
recipes.about: Crunchy carrot sticks with a quick dip of ground peanuts, lime, garlic and a few drops of soy sauce. It's a nutty, tangy, garlicky bite in the spirit of a Vietnamese peanut sauce. The **peanuts add protein and vitamin E**.
steps: Mix the ground peanuts, lime juice, garlic, soy sauce, honey and chili flakes with a splash of warm water, until it is a thick, dippable sauce.
Serve with the carrot sticks.

recipes.name: Crispy sesame-garlic tofu bites
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese pan-fried tofu with garlic and chili
recipes.about: Cubes of tofu pan-fried until golden, then tossed with garlic, chili flakes, a few drops of soy sauce and rice vinegar, and finished with toasted sesame. They're crisp outside, soft inside, and good warm or cold. The **tofu adds protein and calcium**.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, pressed dry and cut into cubes

steps: Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, until golden on most sides, about 7 minutes.

Take the pan off the heat and stir in the garlic and chili flakes; the heat of the pan softens the garlic in about 30 seconds. Add the soy sauce and rice vinegar, toss to coat, then scatter with the sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Warm walnut soy milk with ginger
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese walnut soy milk
recipes.about: Soy milk gently warmed with fresh ginger and a few crushed walnuts, a little sweet and very soothing. It's inspired by the walnut soy milk drinks of northern China. The **soy milk adds protein and calcium** and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then crush them roughly.
Warm the soy milk with the ginger in a small pot over low heat for 5 minutes, without letting it boil. Pour into a mug through a sieve, stir in the honey and top with the walnuts.
recipes.tip: Make a double batch and drink the second one cold.

recipes.name: Ginger-soy marinated egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese ajitsuke tamago and Chinese tea eggs
recipes.about: Hard-boiled egg steeped in a little soy sauce, ginger and star anise. It's savoury, silky and easy to make ahead. The **egg adds protein and choline**.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, until the yolk is firm. Cool them in cold water, then peel.
Put the soy sauce, ginger, star anise and about 60 ml of water per egg in a small zip bag or a snug jar. Add the eggs and leave for at least 4 hours, or overnight, turning them twice.
recipes.tip: Make two at once and double the marinade.

recipes.name: Edamame-ginger dip with carrot sticks
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese edamame-zunda flavours
recipes.about: A thick, green dip of mashed edamame with lime, ginger and a little sesame oil, scooped up with carrot sticks. It's a bright, nutty take on hummus. The **edamame brings protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 4 minutes and drain, saving a splash of the water.
Mash or blend the edamame with the lime juice, ginger, garlic, sesame oil and enough of the water to make a thick dip.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and serve with the carrot sticks.

recipes.name: Quick sesame cucumber and edamame pickle
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese sunomono, with edamame
recipes.about: Cucumber and edamame tossed in rice vinegar, honey, ginger and toasted sesame and left to sit for a few minutes. It's cool, crunchy and tangy, a little like a Japanese sunomono. The **edamame adds protein and fibre**.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and cool.
Whisk the rice vinegar, honey and ginger. Toss with the cucumber and edamame and let it sit for 5 minutes. Scatter with the sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Cucumber and edamame in walnut-miso dressing
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese kurumi-ae (walnut dressing)
recipes.about: Crisp cucumber and edamame tossed in a creamy dressing of toasted ground walnuts, a little miso, rice vinegar and honey. It's a snack version of the Japanese kurumi-ae, nutty, savoury and a touch sweet. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3** and the edamame brings protein.
steps: Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and cool.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then grind them to a coarse paste in a mortar. Stir in the miso, rice vinegar, honey and a splash of water.
Toss the cucumber and edamame with the dressing.
